response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / NULLIF(rental_duration, 0)) AS p FROM film GROUP BY rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(p) AS m FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.p) AS avg_kept_per_day, AVG(r.p - a.m) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.p > a.m

assumptions.assumption: A film's per-day price is rental_rate / rental_duration. A rating's figure is the average of these per-film values, skipping NULLs. Each rating counts equally in the across-rating average.
Films with a NULL rating form their own group. The verified data shows only 5 non-null ratings, so this has no effect here.

alternatives.interpretation: A rating's per-day price is the ratio of totals, SUM(rental_rate) / SUM(rental_duration), instead of the average of per-film ratios.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, SUM(rental_rate) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(rental_duration), 0) AS p FROM film WHERE rental_rate IS NOT NULL AND rental_duration IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), a AS (SELECT AVG(p) AS m FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.p) AS avg_kept_per_day, AVG(r.p - a.m) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.p > a.m
